article.title: Misogynoir of Grift
article.author: Sikivu Hutchinson
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Last week’s Blue Tsunami was a resounding denunciation of the Trump regime’s kleptocratic thievery, thuggery and terrorism, ushering in a groundbreaking cohort of first-time Black, Indigenous, queer, Muslim and female legislators. Post midterms, Democrats have vowed to investigate the Trump family crime syndicate and its brazen trail of corrupt quid pro quo politics, crony capitalism, wage and wealth theft. While large swaths of white middle America unexpectedly turned on Trump and MAGA, communities of color were the driving force for a historic shift in red state alignment. Dems have been given a big fat mandate to redress the economic disenfranchisement of working and middle class people. But any movement to upend corruption must be informed by a reckoning with how misogynoir has greased the wheels of Trump’s epic grift, shafting Black women in record numbers while career criminal oligarchs flourished. One month before the midterms, The New Yorker published an expose of Trump son-in-law Jared Kushner’s monetization of American diplomacy in his so-called unofficial role as a special envoy for the administration. Since his return to office in 2024, Trump has dispatched Kushner to oversee diplomatic negotiations in Iran, Russia and the Middle East. Nepo trust fund sycophant Kushner is exhibit A in a long line of unqualified anti-meritocratic Trump surrogates who have racked up multi-billion dollar paydays by scoring real estate and raw materials deals that enrich the Trump family crime syndicate and its cronies. Related: The Radical King, Claudette Colvin, Patriarchy and Economic Justice According to the New Yorker : “The deals Kushner has assembled in Trump’s second term have made little distinction between personal friends, government associates, and family connections. In September, 2025, he initiated a first round of funding for a startup called Brain Co., which aims to sell A.I. services to businesses and governments. His partner in the venture is Luis Videgaray, the former foreign minister of Mexico, who was his counterpart in negotiating trade agreements during Trump’s first term. Among the funders are the Silicon Valley C.E.O.s Patrick Collison, who gave hundreds of thousands of dollars to Republicans during the 2024 election season, and Brian Armstrong, whose company contributed a million dollars to Trump’s Inauguration fund. In December, Trump signed an executive order limiting states’ ability to regulate A.I.” As the New Yorker notes, “By the standards of this Administration, these conflicts are not extraordinary. David Sacks, one of Trump’s top technology officials, has overseen scores of regulations on A.I. while owning stakes in some five hundred companies tied to the industry.” In the wake of industry warnings about AI’s potential to destroy humanity, Trump has refused to support regulatory controls on the technology. Not surprisingly, his claim that the U.S. would cede AI dominance to China is a smokescreen for his real motive–unbridled profit and unchecked power. While Trump and the kleptocrats have enriched themselves with insider stock trading, crypto deals, land development deals, hospitality industry deals, and arms and oil trades, the white and Latinx MAGA base that cosigned his fascism have seen their economic conditions and quality of life decline precipitously. Latinx men have become leading targets for ICE terrorists. White folks have lost thousands of federal jobs, seen their Medicaid and ACA benefits decimated, while leading the nation in opioid overdose deaths and suicide by gun violence. Now, as data centers, AI slop, and high prices overrun their communities, instead of blaming Blacks, transgender folks and “illegals”, some have finally begun to see the limits of white robber baron kleptocracy because it’s not trickling down to them. The Blue Tsunami voting shift among middle to low income red state whites is unlikely to lead to any critical consciousness about white supremacist privilege and capitalism. Populist or class unrest amongst whites, be it right wing or left wing, has always been informed by the specter of anti-Blackness. Although the divide between the mega rich and working and middle income people of all ethnicities is staggering, the wealth gap between white families and Black families has gotten even wider. According to a 2024 study by the Samuel DuBois Cook Center for Social Equity at Duke University, “The modern racial wealth gap is in fact growing, in large part because of the cumulative impact of the country’s racial history, and intergenerational transfers of wealth from older generations to younger ones.” Related: The Radical King, Claudette Colvin, Patriarchy and Economic Justice It is estimated that Silent Generation and Baby Boomer Americans are sitting on trillions of dollars of wealth represented by investments and home equity. Deep racial disparities in family household wealth remain the number one metric of how entrenched the wages of whiteness are in American society. This has been amplified by the mass layof fs of hundreds of thousands of Black women workers over the past year. As the Economic Policy Institute note s, “In 2025, Black women’s employment rate fell by 1.4 percentage points to 55.7%. This is one of the sharpest one-year declines in the last 25 years (see Figure A). The decline among Black men and white women was no more than 0.5 percentage points each while employment rose slightly for Hispanic (+0.6 percentage points) and AAPI (+0.4 percentage points) women.” Any decline in Black women’s employment rates is devastating for Black communities overall but the targeted job losses of 2025 have been existential. Black women have long had the highest workforce participation of all female demographics in the U.S. Brought here as enslaved labor, the legacies of slavery and Jim Crow made it necessary for Black women to be in the workforce to support their families, be they married or single parents. Moreover , “For decades, the federal government has helped build the Black middle class, offering a relative refuge from pay discrimination by providing transparent wage scales and codified rules on hiring and promotions.” So, when Trump destroyed the federal workforce through layoffs and defunding, Black women with college degrees were disproportionately affected . A recent Washington Post article chronicled the plight of Dia Harris, a Black male former federal employee who was fired from ACF as part of the mass DOGE terminations engineered by Elon Musk. Harris has been targeted and vilified by being featured on a so-called DEI Watchlist website run by the Heritage Foundation. According to the Washington Post , the website’s targets are over two thirds African American. As a result of this harassment, he has been unable to find a living wage job despite having applied to hundreds of positions. Although Harris is male, his situation is similar to that of scores of Black women whose lives were upended by the Trump DOGE employment assault. Not only did Black women lose jobs and wages but retirement, social security and unemployment benefits. Black women-led nonprofits saw their grants rescinded and programming cancelled. Black women who developed and led DEI initiatives at their workplaces were fired in droves as prime victims of Trump and DOGE’s racist, sexist purge. Just as corruption and affordability are priority items for the Democratic congressional supermajority, restoring racial and gender equity in public sector employment and providing pathways to wealth building should also be prioritized–especially for Democratic Socialists who championed economic justice but have been largely silent about white supremacy and racial capitalism. Democrats can and should pass a bill that advances economic and workforce development AND agency reinstatement for Black women, Black men and other vulnerable workers who were unfairly terminated under DOGE. Facilitating equitable access to upskilling, retraining, coaching and job placement for Black workers (who have the highest unemployment overall in the nation) in government and green industries, as well as demanding restoration of federal funding for community-based social justice organizations that were defunded–should also be a mandatory plank in the 2027 Congressional agenda. This agenda must go hand in hand with a push for universal child care. The U.S. is one of the only post-industrial nations without paid child and family leave time. The absence of universal child care is a structural disparity that disproportionately disadvantages Black, Latina and Indigenous women workers due to their lower incomes and heavier caregiving load. Democrats need to jump on these priorities and not treat them as special interest afterthoughts. Black women were crucial to the depth and reach of the Blue Tsunami. Targeted economic, racial and gender justice should be front row and center in a reenergized progressive Democratic agenda to dismantle GOP fascism, white supremacy and grift.
